report:
Reviewed the complete syntax_identities claim, all four implementation associations and both tests. Captured the modules design, Tree-sitter RFD and multifile test/root setup helpers. Source inspection only; no tests rerun and no source changes.

The claim requires syntax-backed stable local identities, owned CST, order/ownership/provenance, downstream semantic work and explicit malformed/unsupported items, with Tree-sitter remaining temporary machinery. parse/mod.rs creates a temporary parse tree and translates its ordered item list into LocalModItemSym values. Syntax errors, unknown top-level kinds and unsupported expression statements become error items instead of accepted definitions; known inert delimiters/comments and cfg-disabled items follow their explicit syntactic handling. parse/items.rs constructs per-item owned stashes and symbols. For example parse_struct builds StructCstData in a new Stash, wraps it in Stashed and constructs LocalStructSym with name/scope/CST/absolute source span. structs.rs separates name/scope identity from tracked CST/span details. mods.rs holds module ownership and parses file-backed children under ScopeSymbol::Module(module); inline children receive their own scoped list. These mechanisms preserve syntax/provenance without publishing Tree-sitter nodes or treating parsing as name/type/trait resolution. Stable identity here is the local Salsa identity model, not a promise of persistent arbitrary edit identity beyond the specified inputs.

The ordinary items_in_a_file_backed_module_use_that_module_as_their_scope test supplies lib.rs with mod child and child.rs with Holder, locates the actual child and struct through expanded membership, and asserts holder.scope equals ScopeSymbol::Module(child). The captured helper loads both files into one database and creates the root parse input. This directly verifies the file-backed ownership regression, but does not check CST self-containment, all provenance/order cases, malformed input or an absence-of-semantic-work trace.

The modules_parse_syntax_identities TODO explicitly retains source/generated fixtures for order, ownership, CST and provenance, error items for malformed/unsupported top-level input, and parse-only traces excluding resolution/signature/body/solver work. Completing that broader matrix is the prerequisite for full verification. It has no assertions and remains deferred; the single file-module scope assertion is not promoted into exhaustive proof of syntax identity stability or all parser boundaries. All implementation and evidence entries and claim aspects are accounted for, no concrete additional defect was identified, and no edits are requested.
